MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JUNE 18, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:02 p.m. at Ernie Howlett Park, 25851 Hawthorne Blvd,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Bain, Persichina, and
  McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Holdsworth

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 21,
  2024

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MAY 21, 2024.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM FUNDING REQUEST
  FROM LOS RANCHOS VERDES HOA

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
June 18, 2024
   Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of the street entryway
  beautification program funding request from the Los Ranchos Verdes HOA (as per
  the agenda material).

  Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed that the budgeted funds available could
  accommodate this project request, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that this program is for formal HOA’s in the City,
  but he would look into how other neighborhoods could be eligible for City funds
  regarding signage, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN. VICE CHAIR
  PERSICHINA stated that he couldn’t recall a neighborhood that was not a formal
  HOA within the City that has tried to apply for this funding program.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE  THE  LOS  RANCHOS  VERDES  HOMEOWNERS
  ASSOCIATION’S REQUEST OF $950 IN MATCHING FUNDS FROM THE
  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM IN FY 2023-24.

  AYES:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Bain, Persichina, McCormick
  ABSENT:  Holdsworth

  B.  REQUEST FOR RECOGNITION OF EQUESTRIAN SHIRLEY KLINE

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the request for recognition of
  equestrian Shirley Kline (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE thanked Peggy Kline for being at the meeting and
  supporting her mother’s accomplishments.

  COMMISSION POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER JOHNSON
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE STAFF RECOMMENDATION TO REQUEST FOR
  APPROVAL BY THE CITY COUNCIL THE PROPOSED EQUESTRIAN
  RECOGNITION PROJECT TO HONOR SHIRLEY KLINE.

  AYES:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Bain, Persichina, McCormick
  ABSENT:  Holdsworth

  C.  PICKLEBALL COURT UTILIZATION UPDATE

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the pickleball court utilization at the
  RHE Tennis Club at Ernie Howlett Park (as per the agenda material).

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
June 18, 2024
   In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Coordinator Morrow shared ideas of how
  new courts designed exclusively for pickleball could potentially be added at the
  tennis club. This included possibly converting the current basketball court to
  pickleball courts and converting the volleyball court to a basketball court.

  In response to CHAIR MCCORMICK, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that if additional
  courts were to be built for pickleball use only, Staff would recommend the pickleball
  overlays on Courts 5 & 6 be removed so those courts could revert to being for
  tennis play only.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the cost to build additional courts is unknown at
  this point and that an assessment would need to be done, in response to
  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA recommended a land stability assessment be
  completed, stating that during an assessment completed previously when a skate
  park was being considered, some portions of the area beyond the volleyball court
  were found to be unstable.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that Staff recommends keeping a basketball court as
  part of any future projects as the current court is often used, in response to CHAIR
  MCCORMICK.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff recommends considering the addition of
  courts to be used exclusively for pickleball while keeping the number of tennis
  courts as currently constructed based on feedback received from pickleball and
  tennis players, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City does charge Chadwick School and the
  other leagues for usage of the courts, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Public comment was provided by Carrie Silvano recommending more pickleball
  courts at the RHE Tennis Club and regarding the growing popularity of pickleball.
  A discussion ensued regarding solutions and ideas for the proposed project based
  on the current pickleball court utilization at the tennis club.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that more information is needed to propose a project
  timeline and that the project is being proposed as a future, long-term solution in
  response to COMMISSIONER BAIN. Supervisor Pinuelas added that Staff is
  looking for grant opportunities to have a consultant conduct an assessment of
  Ernie Howlett Park and its uses, which can be used as a guide for major
  improvements.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by CHAIR MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE RECOMMENDATION BY STAFF TO INCLUDE THE
  ASSESSMENT OF POTENTIAL NEW COURTS EXCLUSIVELY
  DEDICATED TO PICKLEBALL USE AT THE TENNIS CLUB IN THE FY

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
June 18, 2024
   2025-26 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT LIST FOR FUTURE
  CONSIDERATION.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA thanked Staff for their time and effort to ensure the
  safe and proper use of Ernie Howlett Park.

  Coordinator Morrow reported that the Movie Night at the Park event held on June
  8 went well. He noted that Game Truck LA and Battle Party LA provided pre-movie
  activities for those in attendance and that there were approximately 150 people in
  attendance for the movie, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she received feedback from a community
  member at the Palos Verdes Street Fair regarding scheduling the first movie night
  later in the summer. Coordinator Morrow shared that Staff work to coordinate
  summer dates with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes based on their movie night
  and concert in the park schedules as both cities utilize the same vendors for their
  events. He added that Staff would look at possibilities for adjusting the schedule in
  the future.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked about opportunities for vendor participation at
  the movie nights. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that that booth space is currently
  offered at certain sponsorship levels, but that Staff could look into the possibility of
  providing more vendor opportunities.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 28, 2024 ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING/BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
June 18, 2024
   B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 28, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 14, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE UPDATE

  NONE.

  B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT

  NONE.

  C.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked for an update regarding upgrades to the restrooms
  attached to the tennis office building. Coordinator Morrow shared that Staff
  conducted a survey of the tennis club members to gauge their usage of the locker
  room area to see if there was potential to utilize that space to expand and upgrade
  the restrooms. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the majority of those who completed
  the survey stated that they do not use the lockers.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that it is the City’s responsibility to trim the
  branches growing above the Little League snack shack and that Maintenance staff
  planned to trim the branches later that week, in response to VICE CHAIR
  PERSICHINA.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that AYSO was planning to return to Ernie Howlett Park
  for their Fall soccer season and stated that the sloping and grading of the fields
  was the main reason they did not use the fields this past fall season, in response
  to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
June 18, 2024
   Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the City is responsible for the weed
  abatement around the exterior perimeter of the park. He noted that it is completed
  twice a year, and that Maintenance staff and the City’s contracted landscaping
  vendor were about to begin the weed abatement, in response to CHAIR
  MCCORMICK and COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the City has contracted a new gopher control
  vendor and was very pleased with their work so far, in response to VICE CHAIR
  PERSICHINA.

  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that Maintenance staff plan to begin maintenance
  to the trails and walking paths around the horse arenas.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MCCORMICK ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:00 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JULY 16, 2024, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT HIGHRIDGE PARK.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Ryan McCormick
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  6
June 18, 2024
